title: First and last
description: Pick supplies out of the quartermaster's list by their position, and slice off the middle.

tasks.title: Every item has a position
tasks.body: Positions in a list start at 0. In pack = ["rope", "map", "lamp"], pack[0] is "rope" and pack[2] is "lamp". A negative position counts from the end, so pack[-1] is the last item.
tasks.detail: pack[1] = "key" puts a new value at position 1, replacing what was there. A slice such as pack[0:2] is a new list of the items from position 0 up to, but not including, position 2. Asking for a position past the end, like pack[3] here, stops the program with an IndexError.

tasks.code:
# Pick tools from the pack by position
pack = ["rope", "map", "lamp", "key"]
print(pack[0])
print(pack[-1])
print(pack[1:3])
pack[0] = "ladder"
print(pack)
tasks.note: pack[0] is the first item and pack[-1] the last. The slice 1:3 starts at position 1 and stops before 3, so it holds two items. Assigning to pack[0] replaces rope, and the list keeps its length.

tasks.question: With the same four items, what does print(pack[len(pack) - 1]) show?
tasks.why: len(pack) is 4, so len(pack) - 1 is 3, the last position. pack[len(pack)] would be the IndexError: a list of 4 has no position 4.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: add print(pack[4]) and read the error. Then change it to show the last item, in two different ways.

The quartermaster lists the party's supplies. Ask how many supplies there are (always at least 1), then ask for each one, in order. Then ask for a position, counting from 1 the way people do. Print four lines: the first supply, the last supply, the supply at the position asked for, and a list of every supply except the first and the last. Print just those four lines.
tasks.starter: # Ask for the supplies, then a position
hints: Collect the supplies in a list first. Positions start at 0, so the first supply is at 0, and a person who says position 1 means Python position 0.
A negative position counts from the end. A slice gives a list: it starts at its first number and stops just before its second, and either number can be negative.
With other names: name = songs[0] is the first song, name = songs[-1] the last, and the song a person calls number is one position earlier than number.

error_hints.text: A position is past the end of the list. The last item of a list of 4 is at 3, which is also -1, and a person's position 1 is Python's 0.
Positions and range() need whole numbers: turn the number replies into them with int(...).
Your program asked for more replies than it gets. Read the supplies with a loop that runs once per supply, then read the position.
Make the list before the loop uses it, and spell each name the same way every time.
With bread, rope, tent and lamp, and position 2, the lines are bread, lamp, rope and ['rope', 'tent']. If you got tent, the position needs turning into Python's, which starts at 0.
With two supplies there is nothing between the first and the last, so the slice is an empty list, [].
With one supply, it is the first, the last and position 1 all at once.
Check a longer list: the middle slice should keep every supply between the first and the last.
Check position 1: it is the first supply, at Python position 0.

similar_example.note: The same positions in a week: the middle day, the day before last, and a slice from the start, because a slice with no first number starts at 0.

other_ways.code:
count = int(input("How many supplies? "))
supplies = []
for n in range(count):
    supplies.append(input("Supply? "))
position = int(input("Position? "))
print(supplies[0])
print(supplies[len(supplies) - 1])
print(supplies[position - 1])
print(supplies[1:len(supplies) - 1])
other_ways.note: len() - 1 is the last position too. -1 is shorter, and works for a list of any length.

other_ways.code:
count = int(input("How many supplies? "))
supplies = []
for n in range(count):
    supplies.append(input("Supply? "))
position = int(input("Position? "))
print(supplies[0])
print(supplies[-1])
place = 1
for item in supplies:
    if place == position:
        print(item)
    place = place + 1
print(supplies[1:-1])
other_ways.note: Counting along the list the way a person would finds the same supply. Indexing goes straight to it.
